job: Lay a page out as a drafted column cut into bands by hairlines.
purpose: The page holds a centred column with 1px rails; each fd-band is a horizontal strip, separated by hairlines that run edge to edge, with a crosshair where a line meets a rail. Bands set padding, surface and whether they grow. On phones the rails and marks drop away and only the hairlines remain.
useWhen: Any screen in the app: one band for the title, one for the toolbar, one for the content.
A band needs a white or sunken surface, a different padding, or to stick under the top bar.
A public page needs a narrow column of text under a header band: data-column on the band.

avoidWhen.when: Cards or groups inside one band.
Two columns of content inside a band.

states.name: sticky band
states.how: data-sticky; stays under the top bar with a blur

variants.useWhen: The band's children own their padding, as a split does.
48px: empty states and anything that needs room.
A white band that holds tables and inputs.
A recessed band for a quiet area.
With data-grow, centres the content in the band's height.
The last band fills the rest of the height so the rails reach the bottom.
A toolbar band that must stay in view while the page scrolls.
Keep the hairline and drop the crosshairs in a dense area.
A public or signed-out page: the band's content in a centred reading column of 560px under a header band.
A reading column of 320px instead of 560px.
A reading column of 400px instead of 560px.
A reading column of 640px instead of 560px.
A reading column of 768px instead of 560px.
The default reading column of 560px, written out.

parts.role: The main element; a size container named fd-page.
